title: Fields and methods: state and behaviour

videos.script: Lesson 12's book could hold a title and a year, and do nothing else. Every change to it came from outside. This lesson gives a class both halves: what it knows, and what it can do. {{fields}} First the fields. Each object has its own, and each starts with a value even if you never gave it one. Zero, false, or null. {{methods}} Then methods. A method belongs to the class and runs on one object, the one before the dot. It can read that object's fields and change them. {{this}} Inside a method, the word this names that object. You need it when a parameter has the same name as a field. {{constructors}} Last, constructors: the code that runs as an object is made, so that a book is never half built. Write one of your own, and the free one the compiler gave you disappears. By the end, a class carries its data and the rules for changing it, in one place.
